3. The plaint of the plaintiff is, in brief, that the suit land covering an area of 0.24 acres out of 0.97 acres of SA Plot No. 4932 of SA Khatian No. 555 and CS Khatian No. 930 under mouza Bagbhander, PS; Bhurungamari, District-Kurigram was inherited by them from their predecessor Md Hossain Khan who purchased the same from its original owner and possessor Khodeza Khatun by a registered Kabala executed in 1966 on payment of proper consideration. Out of the land of said holdings the said Khodeza Khatun also sold 0.34 acre of land by a registered Kabala dated 14-2-2006 to Md Rustom Ali and his three brothers. Thereafter, three brothers of Md Rustom Ali transferred their share to the said Md Rustom Ali. She also sold 0.08 acre of land to one Yousuf Ali Khan who by a registered deed dated 16-4-1986 transferred his purchased land to his younger brothers Abdus Sattar and Wazed Ali by way of gift, thereafter they sold the said land to the said Md Rustom Ali by a Kabala dated 20-8-1986. Subsequently, the said Khodeza Khatun also sold 0.02 acre of land to one Enayet Hossain. In this manner she transferred 0.68 acre of land from the disputed plot. Thereafter Yousuf Ali Khan transferred 0.05½ acre of land to the said Md Rustom Ali and they have been enjoying and possessing their purchased land. Out of the said purchasers none except late Md Hossain Khan (predecessor of plaintiffs) got possession of actual quantum of land purchased by them, rather they got possession of less quantum since through that land the Assam Access Military Road connecting Shahebgonj to Sonahat, India passes way. It is apparent from the record of Rangpur Collectorate that out of disputed plot 0.58 acres of land was used for construction of the said Assam Access Military Road. The plaintiffs by constructing godown, shops, etc. have been enjoying and possessing the suit land, but the defendant Nos. 1-5 by making obstruction on the way to enter into the plaintiffs land made it useless. On 5th January 1994 the said defendants all on a sudden entered into the suit land and looted away the construction materials collected thereon by the plaintiffs and erected a single roof tin shed measuring 52 x 4 cubits by dis- possessing the plaintiffs forcibly. A criminal case was institutes under sections 147/447/478/379/380 of the Pena: Code against the defendant Nos. 1-7. In the sail Criminal Case the defendant Nos. 1-5 disclosed that the defendant Nos.1-3 purchased 0.04 acre of land from Khodeza Khatun on 7-6-1986. The said Khodeza Khatun by swearing an affidavit before the Magistrate declared that she did not sell any land to the defendant Nos. 1-3 on 7-6-1986. The said Khodeza Khatun had no saleable interest at the time of alleged purchase. Moreover, on that date the defendant Nos. 1-3 were minors. The Kabala on the basis of which the defendants claimed their title in the part of suit land was a benami deed which was not permissible under law and, as such, that kabala has not been acted upon. The plaintiffs as like their predecessor have/had been enjoying and possessing the suit land since 1966. For such dispossession the plaintiff's filed the suit for declaration of their title in the suit land as well as for recovery of the possession in respect of the part from which they were dispossessed and also that the aforesaid Kabala is illegal, void, inoperative and not binding upon them. 

 4. The defendant Nos. 1-3 and their father, the defendant No. 4, contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations and contending that the suit is not maintainable being barred by the principle of waiver, estoppel and acquiescence and by limitation. Their specific case is that the land covering an area of 0.97 acre of the disputed plot admittedly belonged to Khodeza Khatun and the SA record was correctly prepared in her name. Out of the said plot, 0.04 acres of land is situated in front of their residence, and the same was transferred to the defendant Nos. 4 and 5 by the said Khodeza Khatun, they purchased the same in the name of their sons the defendant Nos. 1-3 by the disputed kabala dated 7-6-1986 and got its possession, since then they have been enjoying and possessing the same. The affidavit, as allegedly sworn by Khodeza Khatun, is a fictitious document. She did never swear any such affidavit. The plaintiffs never got possession over that 0.04 acre of land purchased by them. After purchase by erecting tin shed thereon they have been running their business. Though they purchased 0.04 acres of land but they got the possession only in 0.03 acre. Their such purchased land has already been mutated in their names. The plaintiffs have/had no title and possession over that land. It is further contended that the market value of disputed land is not less than Taka 1,50,000 and the suit was not properly valued and stamped. The suit is not maintainable without a prayer for partition. The story of acquisition of land by the Government for construction of road is not correct. There was no such road and the story of acquisition and requisition alleged by the plaintiffs is false. In their additional written statement the said defendants also stated that the land measuring an area of 0.97 acre of the disputed plot and other undisputed land covering an area of 2.07 acre of RS Khatian No. 555 was recorded in the name of Nurun Nabi Sarker. The land of the disputed khatian and other lands originally belonged to Kanai Sheikh under the landlord Goyabari Liton Company Limited. Kanai Sheikh settled the land from disputed and undisputed holding to the said Nurun Nabi Sarker by issuing Dakhila in the last part of 1347 BS. The rent receiving interest of the said landlord Goyabari Liton Company Limited was transferred to one Mohamoyee Dashya and others. After enforcement of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the said Nurun Nabi Sarker became a tenant under the Government and the said Nurun Nabi Sarker transferred the suit land and other lands to Khodeza Khatun from whom the defendants purchased the alleged 0.04 acre.
